doc.title: Ray Drummond interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

title: Closing remarks on struggle and thanks
summary: Rowe wishes him luck; Drummond reflects on being the same age as Dave Holland and Tom Harrell and the struggle to get creative messages out.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well I wish you the best of luck with —
I hope you can focus on some of those projects.

Well you know, que sera sera. I’m 56 years old now and I’m as old as the president, the last two presidents, I’m the same age, we were all born the same year. And Dave Holland I, we’re about a month and a half apart, and Tom Harrell and I are about four months apart, five months apart. So I see all of us trying to — struggling to get our creative messages out.
It’s always some level of struggle.

Yeah. I don’t mind the struggle. The struggle is great. I don’t mind that it’s just that the backdrop in which this struggle continues is one that changes in sometimes unfriendly ways so you always want that backdrop to be at least somewhat — if nothing, at least neutral rather than antagonistic.
Well thanks for your time today.
